title: Anchored Asks and Micro-Commitments — Mira Chen
content:
Purpose: quick, portable notes for manager 1:1 prep and my own half-yearly calibration. Keep concise. Focus on signals managers care about: outcomes, influence, reliability, and partnership.

Topline ask (what I want from this conversation)
- Primary: align on promotion signal and concrete 3-step plan to close gaps by end of Q2 2026.
- Secondary: secure time + sponsorship to lead the cross-team onboarding simplification project (2 months block) and a mentoring slot for one incoming TPM.
- Tertiary: discuss stretch opportunity in product org to co-own onboarding metrics for the next release.

My 3 most important outcomes since last check-in (evidence-focused)
1) Onboarding task force (pilot): reduced mean time-to-first-success from 9.5 days -> 7.8 days (pilot cohort, n=82).
   - My role: designed experiment, facilitated SRE + DXU syncs, drove ship of two small fixes and one docs flow.
   - Signals: adoption of new checklist by 40% of new hires in pilot; tracked via internal onboarding-tracker.
   - Link: JIRA HR-712 (pilot tickets)
2) Offboarding cleanup: closed 18 legacy access tickets, automated 3 steps of the manual checklist saving ~1.6 engineer-hours/week across platform team.
   - Impact: fewer post-offboard incidents in infra on-call (anecdotal, see infra thread).
3) Mentorship & hiring support: ran two interview calibration sessions; mentored one candidate through take-home assignment -> hired as IC level 2.
   - Signal: hiring manager note praising structure and speed of feedback.

Problems I care most about (and why they matter)
- Onboarding friction persists for teams with custom infra (serving-runtime, private-deployments). It scales poorly and increases time to productivity for ramping engineers which slows product velocity.
- Visibility: some of my wins are buried in tickets and slack threads; need better packaging for exec visibility.
- Bandwidth: I'm stretched across tactical cleanup and strategic initiatives — need to frontload focused time to ship the onboarding simplification.

Where I’ve grown / competency signals
- Cross-functional influence: moved from individual task execution to convening and closing across SRE, infra, and DXU. Evidence: two decision memos and a follow-up triage cadence I set up.
- Ownership: I own the onboarding pilot backlog and the offboarding automation cadence.
- Coaching: mentee hit performance bar and team-run calibration shows improved interviewer alignment.

Gaps to address (promotion readiness checklist)
- Metrics ownership: need to define and own 3 measurable metrics and show sustained improvement for at least one quarter (target: reduce time-to-first-success by 20% for next cohort).
- Storytelling: convert ticket-level wins into 1–pager exec readout.
- Scaleable solutions: move from one-off fixes to a platform-level onboarding pattern that can be replicated by other teams.

Concrete next steps (micro-commitments, 2-week cadence)
- This week: draft the onboarding metrics proposal (1 page) and share with you + Lena by Friday. (time block: Tue 90m).
- Next 2 weeks: schedule two 30-min syncs with serving-runtime and private-deployments leads to validate feasibility of the metrics.
- By end of month: produce an exec-ready single-slide summary + one-pager for leadership review.
- 60-day: run A/B of checklist changes across two teams; capture pre/post metrics.

Manager asks (phrased for a short 1:1)
- Priority ask: can you champion this in leadership sync next Wed? I need a signal from you that this is a high-priority cross-team piece.
- Career ask: can we define one stretch deliverable that maps to the promotion rubric (example: lead cross-team onboarding pattern + show metric improvement).
- Support ask: approve 40% time dedicated for 8 weeks for me to lead the pilot (formal carve-out).
- Feedback ask: what is the single biggest remaining gap you see vs. promotion readiness?

Evidence excerpts I want you to cite (copyable bullets in 1:1)
- "Designed and shipped onboarding pilot that reduced mean time-to-first-success from 9.5 -> 7.8 days for pilot cohort (n=82)."
- "Automated 3 manual offboarding steps reducing weekly manual effort and lowering post-offboard incidents reported by infra."
- "Led interview calibration and mentorship that converted a candidate to hire; improved interviewer alignment."

Risks / counterpoints I anticipate
- Metrics wobble: pilot cohort could be statistically noisy; need longer run to claim improvement.
- Resource pushback: leadership may not want to allocate dedicated headcount/time.
- Competing priorities: Product org timeline may shift, delaying shared work.

Notes to myself (talking points / quick scripts)
- If asked "why you?": emphasize convening track record, concrete results, and existing relationships with infra/DXU.
- If asked "how will this scale?": propose a repeatable checklist + templated onboarding flow and owner playbook.
- If asked "what success looks like?": 20% reduction in time-to-first-success in Q2 cohort + adoption of checklist by 50% of new hires in target teams.

Open questions / TODOs (short)
- Confirm whether we can use product telemetry bucket for cohort tracking (ask data infra).
- Check if hiring budget includes a matching mentor bonus for time spent (comp/people ops).
- Draft exec one-pager and run by Arpita for tone/metrics.

Tiny experiments to try (low effort)
- Add "first-success" micro-survey to onboarding checklist to capture a self-reported signal (1-question, NPS-like).
- Two-week office hours slot for new hires: 30 minutes on Fridays, test adoption.

Archive / reference snippets (links I want to include in final one-pager)
- Pilot result dashboard (not public yet) — will paste link after data infra confirmation.
- JIRA HR-712 (tickets + experiment notes)
- Slack thread: #onboarding-pilot (high-level comments by product owners)

Mood / micro-reflection
- Feeling energized when I see cross-team momentum; frustrated when wins sit in tickets.
- My narrative goal: be the person who takes messy operational problems and turns them into repeatable, measurable patterns.

End note: keep this doc short and iterative. Update after 1:1 and tag what we committed.
